text.p: The dollar fluctuated within slim session ranges in late Europe as the market remained hamstrung ahead of the week's only major U.S. data release.
Friday sees the appearance of U.S. September producer prices and retail sales, with operators eager for clues on whether or not a Federal Reserve rate hike could be in the pipeline.

U.S. data out today surprised the market with their strength. Jobless claims fell to 319,000 in the October 5 week, confounding expectations of little change from the previous week's 341,000. Analysts said the data were significant because claims usually rose in the first week of the new quarter.

"This emphasises the strength of the labour markets in the States. It's yet another indication that the September employment report was distorted downwards by faulty seasonal adjustment," said Stuart Thomson, chief international economist at Nikko Europe in London.
The dollar was quoted at 1.5292/95 marks and 111.23/28 yen by 1508 GMT compared to late Wednesday's late European levels of 1.5282/87 and 111.46/51.
The Bundesbank surprised few by leaving its official interest rates unchanged after its regular council meeting. The next two repo tenders were set at an unchanged 3.0 percent.
The dollar spiked up briefly in Asia overnight after unfounded rumours of Russian President Boris Yeltsin's death gripped the market.
In the UK, Chancellor Kenneth Clarke was acclaimed by his Conservative colleagues after addressing their party conference, despite making no firm pledges to cut taxes.
Sterling also reacted positively to Clarke's speech, in which he said the Conservatives would only reduce taxes when they could afford to and when it was good for the economy.
The basic rate of income tax would eventually fall to 20 percent from the current 24 percent, Clarke said.
Clarke also said he would "get and keep" core inflation below 2.5 percent, a claim undermined somewhat by new figures showing UK September retail prices rose more than expected.
RPI came in up 0.5 percent on the month for a year-on-year increase of 2.1 percent, above the 2.0-percent forecast. Core inflation, or RPIX, was at 2.9 percent versus the expected 2.8.
Sterling was quoted at 2.3940/45 marks and $1.5651/56 by 1527 GMT against late Wednesday's 2.3912/15 and $1.5643/53.
Elsewhere, the dollar was little changed against the Swiss franc at 1.2520/26 francs versus late yesterday's 1.2528/33.
